description: Use when the question is 'which country is best/safest/cheapest for X' or any ranked multi-country comparison — e.g. 'compare Portugal vs Paraguay vs UAE for relocation', 'safest low-tax countries', 'rank countries by cost of living and banking access'. Scores jurisdictions on an 8-dimension weighted model (tax, safety, healthcare, institutions, business_ease, privacy, cost_of_living, banking_access). Pass `countries` (2–50 ISO-3166 codes or English names) to compare a specific set, or omit to rank all available countries (cap with `limit`). Pass `weights` (0–100 per dimension) to match the user's stated priorities. The `tax` score reflects how an individual's crypto is taxed, not salary income tax. `tax_basis` on each row gives the estimate it is computed from and the source's two rule wordings (capital gains, income on crypto): when a wording is a range or has conditions the score rests on an estimate, so quote the wording. Where that estimate is 0%, `zero_tax_rate` on the row says whether the zero is `firm` (scores 10) or `conditional` (holds only under conditions such as a holding period or foreign-source income; scores 9.5), so check get_crypto_tax_treatment before quoting a conditional zero; it is null for any other estimate. The overall `score` is led by the crypto tier, so a row can outrank another with a better `tax` score. For goal-driven relocation shortlists that also weigh residency terms, crypto-tax tier, and passport power, use optimize_relocation instead.

countries.description: 2-50 countries to compare, each an ISO-3166 alpha-2/alpha-3 code or English name, e.g. ['PT', 'Paraguay', 'UAE']. Omit to rank every country.

limit.description: How many countries to return when `countries` is omitted (default 20).

weights.description: Importance of each dimension, 0-100: tax, safety, healthcare, institutions, business_ease, privacy, cost_of_living, banking_access. Omitted dimensions keep their default weight.
